help.alignment: Last 5 minutes, proxy vs. engine: Proxy requests = requests the gateway forwarded to this deployment; Engine completed = requests the engine reports as finished successfully; Client errors = 4xx and 429 (the caller's fault); Server errors = 5xx and asleep-503; In flight = requests the proxy has dispatched that are still open at the end of the window; Lost = proxy requests minus completed and errored ones - shown in red only when more requests are missing than could have been in flight at any point in the window.
help.latency: TTFT = from a request's arrival to its first output token; end-to-end = from arrival to the end of the reply. p50 is the mean of each 10s median in the window; p95/p99 are the maximum of each 10s quantile in the window, a conservative upper bound rather than one quantile over the whole window. The engine's values are used when it reports them; when it does not (an engine without /metrics), the gateway's are, and the gateway's TTFT and end-to-end count from the request reaching an instance, queueing and the network included.
help.tpot: TPOT = the time per output token in decode; lower is faster, and 1000 ÷ TPOT is roughly one stream's output tokens per second. p95/p99 are the maximum of each 10s quantile in the window, a conservative upper bound. When the engine reports no TPOT (TensorFold, Strata), the gateway measures it: for each streamed reply, the time from the first generated token the gateway receives to the last, averaged over the output tokens, network jitter included.
help.concurrency: Per replica: Running = requests currently being decoded by the engine; Waiting = requests queued inside the engine that have not started prefill. Waiting rising while Running is flat means the engine is at its concurrency or KV cache limit.
help.kv: Per replica: Usage % = share of the engine's KV cache blocks in use (near 100% forces preemption or queueing); Hit rate % = share of prompt tokens served from the prefix cache instead of being recomputed.
help.throughput: Per replica: Prompt tok/s = prompt (input) tokens processed per second during prefill; Generation tok/s = output tokens produced per second during decode.
help.stage_time: queue = wait from a request entering the engine until prefill starts; prefill = time processing the prompt before the first token; decode = time generating the whole output after the first token (it grows with the output; per-token speed is TPOT). Each is a single request's duration, the maximum of the per-10-second p95 within the window - a conservative upper bound. When the engine exports no such histograms, the times the engine reports in each reply are aggregated instead; a stage the replies do not carry is not drawn (TensorFold reports prefill and decode only).
help.preemptions: Requests per second the engine evicted from the running set (KV cache pressure) and re-queued. Every preemption re-runs prefill for that request, so a sustained non-zero rate inflates TTFT and wastes compute.
help.replicas: One row per instance of this deployment: engine-side concurrency, KV cache and token throughput, plus per-GPU utilization, memory bandwidth, temperature and power from the node's collector. Click a row to open the instance in Inference Services.
help.pd: PD effectiveness = the share of the decode instances' prompt tokens that arrived by KV transfer rather than being recomputed; fallback rate = requests the decode instances served alone, with the top reasons; the prefill stage (mean / p95) is how long the gateway waited for the prefill instance, and the prefill queue tells whether the prefill instances keep up; the KV transfer comes from the engine's own transfer metrics, per transfer rather than per request: time, size and rate from the decode instances; failed counts the decoders' failed KV pulls; expired counts requests whose KV a prefill instance released because no decoder pulled it before its lease ran out (30 s by default in vLLM 0.30, renewed once a decoder holds the request): the request never reached a decoder after its prefill (the client left, the hand-off failed) or the decode instance failed; the mean prompt length flags loads too short to gain from disaggregation.

requests.title: Requests
requests.help: Each row is one request through the gateway: who sent it, its size, and its phases as a bar of its own duration. Before the first token the gateway sees one wait; when the engine reports per-request stats (vLLM with --enable-per-request-metrics, TensorFold, Strata) a finished request's wait is split into the engine's queue and prefill. Hover or focus a row for times and speeds.

drawer.title: Request details
drawer.observationScope: These records describe what GPUWorks observed. A successful gateway write does not prove that a third-party gateway delivered the response to the final client.
drawer.streamingEvidence: For streaming requests, finish_reason describes the model completion; it does not prove that data: [DONE] was received. Enable debug collection before reproducing, then compare the upstream and client-direction bytes and the terminal read/write errors in the diagnostic bundle.

latency.title: End-to-end latency breakdown
latency.help: The end-to-end time of the whole replies (completed, or stopped at the output limit) in the range, split by the phases the requests went through. Each segment is the phase's mean (0 for a request without it), so the segments add up to the end-to-end mean. When the engine reports its prefill (vLLM with per-request metrics, TensorFold, Strata) it is split out of the wait before the first token, and so is the queue when reported too (vLLM); what is not split stays one wait. Gateway is the gateway's own measured forwarding time; engine preprocessing, shown when the engine reports its queue, is the part of the wait before the first token the engine did not account for (tokenizing, waiting for the step it is running to end, the first token's trip back, network included), and grows under load. Hover a segment for its p50 / p95 and mean speed.

health.title: Health
health.help: Every minute the server sends the service one minimal request through the gateway (a chat model gets the message "1" and generates 1 token, an embedding model embeds "1"); a reply within the threshold is healthy. The strip is the last 10 checks, oldest on the left. The check only reports: it triggers nothing and is not counted in the request figures. Below are the replicas running against those wanted, and each replica's state.
health.enable: Turn it on for the deployment

live.title: Requests in flight
live.help: The requests being served now, counted by phase: waiting for the first token (queue and prefill, which the gateway cannot tell apart before the end), thinking, answering. Refreshed every 2 seconds.
live.longestWait: longest wait for a first token {{time}}
live.swimlaneHelp: Each dot is a request being served, on its phase's lane, placed by how long it has been in flight (log scale). Dots crowding the right of the waiting lane mean a queue; a lone dot far from the rest is a stuck request; a red ring marks one that has sent nothing new for over 2 seconds. Hover for whose request it is and which replica serves it.
live.drawnLongest: {{count}} in flight; the {{drawn}} most worth a look are drawn (longest waits first)
